The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words:

[4] ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years.﴾

His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: That is, the angels and the Spirit, who is Jibril, ascend to Him, Mighty and Majestic, in a Day whose measure for their ascent is that, while for other creatures it is fifty thousand years. That is because they ascend from the lowest extent of the earth to the highest extent of His command above the seven heavens.

It has also been said: Rather, its meaning is: the angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day in which He finishes judging among His creatures, and the measure of that Day on which the judgment among them was finished is fifty thousand years.

It has also been said that "in a Day" is connected to "occurring" (wāqi'), and that what is meant by it is the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn 'Abbas related: It is the Day of Resurrection, which Allah made, for the disbelievers, the measure of fifty thousand years. The stated measure is either literal, or a metaphor for prolongation.

Al-Shihab said: Likewise is the time of every hardship, as it has been said:

Enjoy the days of happiness, for they are short,
while the days of sorrow are long.

Al-Razi related from Abu Muslim that this Day is the Day of the whole worldly life, from the first thing Allah created until the end of annihilation. Thus He, the Exalted, made clear that in the Day of the worldly life there must be the ascent and descent of the angels, and this Day is measured at fifty thousand years. Then it does not follow from this that the time of the Resurrection becomes known, because we do not know how much has passed and how much remains. End of quotation. This is far-fetched. And this verse is like the verse: ﴿He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth; then it ascends to Him in a Day the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count.﴾ [al-Sajdah: 5]

(p-5926) There is no contradiction in the measure, because what is intended by it is prolongation, due to its severity upon the disbelievers, or due to the multitude of states and reckonings that occur in it. The Qur'an explains one part of it by another. And Allah knows best.

On the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[22–35] ﴿Except those who pray, who are constant in their prayer﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 23], ﴿and those in whose wealth there is a known right﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 24], ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 25], ﴿and those who affirm the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 26], ﴿and those who are apprehensive of the punishment of their Lord﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 27], ﴿indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not something to be felt secure from﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 28], ﴿and those who guard their private parts﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 29], ﴿except from their spouses or what their right hands possess, for indeed they are not blameworthy﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 30], ﴿but whoever seeks beyond that, it is they who are the transgressors﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 31], (p-5929) ﴿and those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenant﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 32], ﴿and those who stand firm in their testimonies﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 33], ﴿and those who guard their prayers﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 34], ﴿those will be in gardens, honoured﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 35].

﴿Except those who pray﴾ ﴿who are constant in their prayer﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 23]: that is, they maintain it, neglecting none of it.

﴿And those in whose wealth there is a known right﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 24] ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 25]: that is, the one who abstains (al-mutaʿaffif) from whom the world has turned away, so that he does not ask people. It was said: the one whose wealth does not grow. It was said: the one whose produce has been struck by calamity, drawing on the words of the people of the Garden in the surah before: ﴿Rather, we are deprived﴾ [al-Qalam: 27]. The wording is more general than all of that.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Umar that he was asked whether the known right was the zakat, and he said: "Indeed, upon you are rights other than that."

Similarly from Ibn Abbas, who said: "It is other than the charity, by which one joins the ties of kinship, or hosts a guest, or carries a burden, or helps one who is deprived."

From al-Sha'bi: "Indeed, in wealth there is a right other than zakat."

﴿And those who affirm the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 26]: that is, the recompense.

﴿And those who are apprehensive of the punishment of their Lord﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 27]. Ibn Jarir said: that is, fearful that He will punish them in the Hereafter, so out of fear of that they neglect none of His obligations and transgress none of His limits.

﴿Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not something to be felt secure from﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 28]: that is, that it may befall one who disobeys Him and opposes His command.

﴿And those who guard their private parts﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 29]: that is, owing to the dominance of the faculty of patience and their mastery over its forelock. (p-5930)

﴿Except from their spouses or what their right hands possess, for indeed they are not blameworthy﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 30] ﴿but whoever seeks beyond that, it is they who are the transgressors﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 31]. Ibn Jarir said: that is, he seeks a place for his private part other than his wife or what his right hand possesses.

﴿Then it is they who are the transgressors﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 31]: that is, those who exceed what Allah has made lawful for them to what He has forbidden to them.

﴿And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenant﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 32]. Ibn Jarir said: that is, [faithful to] the trusts of Allah which He entrusted them with from His obligations, and the trusts of His servants which they were entrusted with, and His covenants which He took from them to obey Him in what He commanded them and forbade them, and the covenants of His servants which He gave them, in accordance with what He has pledged for them on His own self; they watch over that, observe it, and do not neglect it.

﴿And those who stand firm in their testimonies﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 33]: that is, they do not conceal what they are called to testify to, but they stand up to render it wherever its rendering is obligatory for them, without altering or changing it.

﴿And those who guard their prayers﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 34]: that is, they neglect neither its appointed times nor its limits. It was said: "guarding" (hifz) is protection from loss, and it has been borrowed for completing and perfecting its pillars and forms. Hence al-Qadi said: the repetition of the mention of prayer and describing them with it at the beginning and the end is for two considerations: to indicate its excellence and its superiority over other acts.

﴿Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not something to be felt secure from﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 28]: that is, that it may befall one who disobeys Him and opposes His command.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 70, verses 40–44:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[40–44] ﴿So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests that We are able﴾ ﴿to replace them with better than them, and We are not to be outdone﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 41] ﴿So leave them to wade in falsehood and play until they meet their Day which they are promised﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 42] ﴿The Day they will emerge from the graves quickly, as if they were rushing toward a idol they were making for﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 43] ﴿with humbled eyes, covered by humiliation. That is the Day which they were promised﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 44]

﴿So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests﴾ means the east and west of every day of the year, or the east and west of every star, or the regions in which the sun rises and sets.

﴿Indeed We are able﴾ ﴿to replace them with better than them, and We are not to be outdone﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 41] meaning: not overcome, if We wish that.

﴿So leave them to wade in falsehood and play until they meet their Day which they are promised﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 42] meaning: their being seized in it and their destruction.

﴿The Day they will emerge from the graves quickly, as if they were rushing toward a idol they were making for﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 43] meaning: they will hasten.

And (al-Nusub) (the idol) is the statue set up for worship, or the marker set up on the road so that the traveller may be guided by it, or that which is set up as a sign of the descent and passage of a king. So they will hasten as idol-worshippers hasten toward their idol, or as one who has lost his way hastens toward its markers, or as soldiers hasten toward the banner of the commander.

﴿with humbled eyes﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 44] meaning: from disgrace and humiliation.

﴿covered by humiliation﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 44] meaning: humiliation envelops them from the terror of what has befallen them.

﴿That is the Day which they were promised﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 44] meaning: that they would meet it.
